messages.subject: How to use "expand_range"
parts:
I have a plotarea (call to ggplot and data below) where I need som
extra space to the right in order to plot text labels. If I use
something like "expand=c(0,1)" I get extra space both to the right and
to the left. - Which is not what I want.

In the documentation I found this "convenience function for expanding
a range with a multiplicative or additive constant."

expand_range(range, mul = 0, add = 0, zero = 0.5)

is this something that might help? I guess I could set zero to some
value >0.5 in order to achieve what I want, but I cant figure out how
to use expand_range?

Thanks in advance

messages.subject: Re: How to use "expand_range"
parts:
> Don't use expand_range - use xlim.

Sorry - but how exactly would you do this with scale_x_discrete?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: How to use "expand_range"
parts:
>> Don't use expand_range - use xlim.
>
> Sorry - but how exactly would you do this with scale_x_discrete?

I didn't realise you had a discrete x axis. You can work around it as follows:

xscale <- scale_x_discrete()
xscale$train(5.5) # if you had 5 levels
